topStories.headline: Excelsior Landmark Pharmacy Building Sold — Future Unclear as New Owners Eye Office Use
topStories.dek: The 117-year-old Central Drug Store building on Mission Street has been sold to a San Bruno plumbing company, leaving the neighborhood wondering what comes next.
topStories.body:
The longtime home of Central Drug Store — a 117-year-old independent pharmacy at 4494 Mission St. at Santa Rosa Avenue that permanently closed last July — has been sold to new owners Markopulos Fotiu and Silvi Palloj, who have operated Marco Polo Plumbing out of San Bruno for 15 years. The sale was completed in June 2026, according to city records.

A building permit approved on July 1 references the construction of new office space under the Marco Polo Plumbing name, and the address has been administratively changed to 10 Santa Rosa Ave. The city's Office of Small Business confirmed through program and communications manager Michelle Lynch Reynolds that there is no rule requiring the space to remain a pharmacy.

When asked about plans for the building, owner Fotiu declined to share details, telling Mission Local, "We haven't made a decision what it is gonna be." He did note a personal connection to the area: "We know the area. Grew up in the area."

The closure of Central Drug Store — which served Excelsior residents for generations — was lamented as a blow to the neighborhood's working-class, immigrant character. For now, the future of one of the Excelsior's most recognizable storefronts remains unresolved.

topStories.headline: Community Groups Raise Alarm Over Two Planned Data Centers Near Bayview–Hunters Point
topStories.dek: Residents and Supervisor Shamann Walton are pushing back against data centers proposed for one of San Francisco's most environmentally overburdened neighborhoods.
topStories.body:
Reporter JR Valrey of the San Francisco Bay View has raised the alarm about two planned data centers near Bayview–Hunters Point and Visitacion Valley, with concerns centering on additional pollution, water use, and the lack of community input on projects that moved forward without public notice. Supervisor Shamann Walton has said the projects advanced without community engagement and that legislative action may be warranted.

One of the centers, a 182,000-square-foot facility developed by Novva, was slated to become active in Bayview before the end of summer 2026, according to reporting from Opgov News. A separate large data center, operated by Digital Reality, is located at 200 Paul Avenue in the Bayview. Novva has described its center as the "greenest data center ever created in the area," citing the use of hydrotreated vegetable oil as biofuel and a waterless cooling system.

Environmental justice advocates argue the clustering of data centers disproportionately affects the Black, Latine, and Asian American Pacific Islander residents who make up the majority of BVHP's population. The neighborhood already carries one of the heaviest pollution burdens in California, shaped by the legacy of the Hunters Point Naval Shipyard Superfund site and decades of industrial zoning.

Community members and organizers are calling for formal environmental review and mandatory community benefit agreements before any additional industrial data infrastructure is permitted in the neighborhood.

topStories.headline: Bayview Oyster Bar Set to Open on Third Street, Anchoring Neighborhood's Restaurant Revival
topStories.dek: Bayview native April Spears is preparing to open her fourth restaurant on Third Street, adding a raw bar and Louisiana-style seafood to a corridor that has seen a wave of new eateries in 2025–26.
topStories.body:
Bayview native and veteran restaurateur April Spears is preparing to open Bayview Oyster Bar at 5114 3rd St., with a debut expected in September 2026, according to the San Francisco Chronicle. The restaurant will feature a raw bar at the front, a seafood counter, about 25 dining seats, and an eventual backyard patio, and will be decorated with historic photographs of Bayview from the 1950s and '60s.

The menu will combine Northern California seafood — including Dungeness crab, king salmon, and oysters — with Spears' Louisiana roots, with some dishes prepared over open flames in a New Orleans-inspired style. The restaurant is one of nine businesses receiving support through the city's Storefront Opportunity Grant program, which offers $100,000 to qualifying full-service restaurants and bars.

Spears previously ran Auntie April's Chicken, Waffles & Soul Food for 15 years and the cocktail lounge Cafe Envy, both of which closed during the pandemic. Bayview Oyster Bar will be her fourth restaurant in her native neighborhood. The Bayview has struggled economically in recent years — from 2019 to 2025, the corridor saw a 31 percent decline in sales tax revenue — but a wave of city-supported openings, including Smoke Soul Kitchen, Frank Grizzly's, and Sco's in 2025, signals renewed momentum on Third Street.

events.title: Sunday Streets Bayview 2026
events.location: Lane Street between Thomas and Underwood Avenues, Bayview
events.description: San Francisco's free open-streets festival returns to the Bayview for a day of car-free fun on Lane Street, featuring a Kids Zone hosted by the Bayview YMCA, live music, active play, health resources, and community vendors. SFMTA's Bayview Community Pathway team will also be on hand to gather public input on the neighborhood's new active-transportation corridor.

events.title: Visitacion Valley Night Market & Block Party
events.location: Leland Ave between Bayshore Blvd and Peabody St, Visitacion Valley
events.description: The inaugural Visitacion Valley Night Market takes over Leland Avenue with food vendors, local shopping, live music by DJ Cilla and Native Elements, street dancing, family-friendly activities, and community resources — all free. The event repeats on September 25.

events.title: Hunters Point Shipyard Open Studios — Fall 2026
events.location: Hunters Point Shipyard, 451 Galvez Ave, Bayview
events.description: Over 100 artists open their working studios at one of the nation's largest artist communities, featuring paintings, sculpture, ceramics, jewelry, photography, and more, plus live music, food, and a beer and wine garden. Free admission and parking with RSVP; fall dates are October 18–19.
events.sourceName: Hunters Point Shipyard Artists / Shipyard Trust for the Arts

events.title: Sunday Streets Excelsior 2026
events.description: Sunday Streets returns to the Excelsior for the final event of the 2026 season, transforming neighborhood streets into car-free community space with free activities, live music, health resources, and local vendors for all ages.

moreNews.headline: SFMTA's Bayview Community Pathway Heads to Sunday Streets for Public Input
moreNews.body: The SFMTA's Bayview Community Pathway project — a planned north-south active transportation corridor parallel to Third Street, featuring protected bikeways, raised crosswalks, bulb-outs, and traffic calming — will host a community engagement pop-up at Sunday Streets Bayview on August 23 from 12–5 p.m. Residents can weigh in on decorative crosswalk designs and view a pedestrian plaza demonstration. The project was officially approved in December 2025 and encompasses segments of Mendell Street, Newcomb Avenue, Lane Street, Underwood Avenue, and Keith Street.

moreNews.headline: India Basin Waterfront Park Presses Toward 2028 Completion as Final Shoreline Phase Continues
moreNews.body: India Basin Waterfront Park at 900 Innes Ave in Bayview–Hunters Point continues to open to the public even as crews work on the final phase of construction, which the San Francisco Recreation and Parks Department says is expected to run through early 2028. The 900 Innes parcel already features two new public piers, a floating dock, ADA-compliant Bay Trail access, a food pavilion, and a makers' shop for boat-building and community programs. Partners have raised more than $186 million toward an approximately $200 million goal. The full 10-acre park will close a critical gap in the San Francisco Bay Trail and will include restoration of the historic 1875 Shipwright's Cottage as a community space and mini museum.

moreNews.headline: U3Fit Gym Expands to Major New Bayview Location Ahead of 2027 Opening
moreNews.body: Lawanda Dickerson, owner of the popular U3Fit gym at 4646 Third St. in Bayview, has leased a new, approximately 20,000-square-foot facility at 1610 Armstrong Ave., which she says will be the largest health and fitness center in Bayview outside of the neighborhood YMCA. Dickerson expects to open the expanded location in 2027. The news, reported in Mission Local's April 2026 Bayview Buzz column, signals continued investment in wellness infrastructure on the Third Street corridor.

restaurants.name: Old Skool Cafe
restaurants.type: Jazz supper club & soul food restaurant
restaurants.description: A 1920s-themed speakeasy jazz supper club staffed by at-risk and formerly incarcerated youth ages 16–22, serving Southern and global soul food with live music nightly.

restaurants.name: Gumbo Social
restaurants.description: A beloved farmers-market-pop-up-turned-brick-and-mortar on Third Street serving deeply flavored gumbos, po'boys, and sides with a build-your-own hot-sauce wall.

restaurants.name: Smoke Soul Kitchen
restaurants.description: A minority- and woman-owned counter-service soul food spot in the former Auntie April's space, celebrated for fried chicken and waffles, biscuit sandwiches, and shrimp and grits.

restaurants.name: Gratta Wines
restaurants.type: Urban winery, wine bar & Italian specialty market
restaurants.description: A neighborhood institution since 2006, Gratta produces small-batch wines from Dry Creek grapes in a Bayview garage winery and serves them alongside Italian comfort food and specialty market items.

restaurants.name: Excelsior Coffee
restaurants.description: A community-minded coffee shop on Mission Street serving espresso drinks, ube pastries, and rotating food items, owned and operated by Excelsior residents.

restaurants.name: Tala Wine
restaurants.description: A boutique natural wine bar on Mission Street with a carefully curated list of low-intervention imports, snack plates, artisan teas, and regular winemaker tasting events.

restaurants.name: Taqueria Guadalajara
restaurants.description: A no-frills Excelsior taqueria with fast service, excellent made-to-order burritos in multiple styles, and an array of proteins including lengua, cabeza, and carne asada.

restaurants.name: Ty Sandwich
restaurants.description: A takeout-only Excelsior gem serving forearm-sized bánh mì stuffed with marinated meats, fresh herbs, and crunchy vegetables, plus a lengthy boba tea menu.

restaurants.name: Beijing Restaurant
restaurants.description: A quick-service Excelsior spot specializing in Beijing-focused dishes with an extensive menu of northern Chinese comfort food at accessible prices.

restaurants.name: Soo Fong Restaurant
restaurants.description: A longtime Bayview Chinese restaurant near Third Street favored by locals for consistent, affordable Cantonese-style dishes.

restaurants.name: Burma Bear
restaurants.description: A Yelp-rated favorite in Bayview–Hunters Point offering Burmese comfort dishes in a welcoming neighborhood setting.

restaurants.name: Mission Rock Resort
restaurants.description: A sprawling waterfront bar and restaurant at the Third Street bridge offering bay views, an expansive deck, seafood, and American staples popular with the after-work crowd.
restaurants.address: 817 China Basin St, San Francisco, CA 94107

restaurants.name: All Good Pizza
restaurants.description: A community-focused pizzeria at Jerrold and Third Street in Bayview known for good-value pies and proximity to the Saturday farmers market.

restaurants.name: Let's Eat BBQ & More
restaurants.description: A locally owned Bayview barbecue spot praised by neighborhood regulars for personable service and satisfying smoked meats.

restaurants.name: Constanso's
restaurants.description: A Bayview deli open into the evening and popular with locals for its affordable, hearty sandwiches and quick service on Third Street.

shops.name: Flora Grubb Gardens
shops.description: An acclaimed 8,000-square-foot open-air garden center and design shop in Bayview specializing in drought-tolerant plants, succulents, and outdoor accessories, with an on-site coffee counter.

shops.name: Gratta Wines Market
shops.description: Attached to the Gratta Wines tasting room, this specialty market stocks Italian pantry items, cured meats, artisan cheeses, and Gratta's own estate-produced wines for retail purchase.

shops.name: Excelsior Coffee (retail)
shops.description: In addition to its café service, Excelsior Coffee sells bags of beans to go and retail pastries, anchoring the Mission Street commercial strip as a community gathering point.

shops.name: Tala Wine (retail)
shops.description: Beyond its bar service, Tala Wine Co. stocks a carefully curated retail selection of natural, low-intervention wines available by the bottle for takeaway.

artEntertainment.name: Bayview Opera House Ruth Williams Memorial Theatre
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's oldest theater, founded in 1888 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places, operated as a community cultural center offering arts classes, youth programs, music, dance, and cultural events on Third Street.

artEntertainment.name: Hunters Point Shipyard Artists Studios (HPSA)
artEntertainment.description: The nation's largest artist collective, with more than 250 artists working in studios at the historic Hunters Point Shipyard; open to the public twice yearly for free Spring and Fall Open Studios weekends.

artEntertainment.name: Shipyard Gallery (Building 101)
artEntertainment.description: The main gallery space within the Hunters Point Shipyard Artists complex, hosting rotating exhibitions of work by the 250+ resident artists during open studios and special events.
artEntertainment.address: 451 Galvez Ave, Bldg 101, San Francisco, CA 94124

artEntertainment.name: Jerry Garcia Amphitheater
artEntertainment.description: A Greek-style outdoor amphitheater in John McLaren Park with a capacity of 1,200, named for the Grateful Dead guitarist who grew up in the Excelsior, hosting free concerts and community performances after a $1.5 million renovation.
artEntertainment.address: John McLaren Park, San Francisco, CA 94134

artEntertainment.name: India Basin Waterfront Park
artEntertainment.description: Bayview's new marquee 10-acre waterfront park at 900 Innes Ave featuring piers, a floating dock, a food pavilion, and rotating arts and cultural programming under an Equitable Development Plan designed by and for the Bayview community.

artEntertainment.name: Quesada Gardens
artEntertainment.description: A vibrant community-transformed public garden at Quesada and Newhall featuring colorful murals, tiled stairs, and lush green space that has served as a Bayview gathering place since 2006.
artEntertainment.address: Quesada Ave at Newhall St, San Francisco, CA 94124

gymsRecreation.name: Bayview Hunters Point YMCA
gymsRecreation.description: A full-service YMCA on Lane Street in the heart of Bayview offering fitness facilities, indoor and outdoor pools, sports courts, youth programs, and after-school education in partnership with SFUSD.

gymsRecreation.name: U3Fit
gymsRecreation.description: A popular small gym on the Third Street corridor owned by life and fitness coach Lawanda Dickerson, serving Bayview residents with personalized training and community-focused fitness programming.

gymsRecreation.name: Excelsior Yoga
gymsRecreation.description: A Mission Street yoga studio on the third floor of the US Bank Building offering 90-minute classical Hatha yoga classes at three levels, plus restorative bodywork including Seifukujutsu massage and Reiki.
gymsRecreation.address: 4610 Mission St, Fl 3, San Francisco, CA 94112

gymsRecreation.name: Love and Light Yoga and Wellness
gymsRecreation.description: A Latina-owned boutique studio on Mission Street in the Excelsior offering all-level Vinyasa, Power Flow, Slow Flow, Yin Yoga, Barre, Mat Pilates, and Zumba, plus sound baths and a 200-hour teacher training program.

gymsRecreation.name: John McLaren Park
gymsRecreation.description: San Francisco's second-largest park, straddling the Excelsior, Crocker Amazon, and Visitacion Valley neighborhoods, with more than 7 miles of trails, a golf course, Coffman Pool, the Jerry Garcia Amphitheater, six playgrounds, tennis courts, basketball courts, baseball diamonds, and McNab Lake.
gymsRecreation.address: John F. Shelley Dr, San Francisco, CA 94134

gymsRecreation.name: India Basin Waterfront Park (Recreation)
gymsRecreation.type: Waterfront park with Bay Trail access
gymsRecreation.description: A new 10-acre waterfront park in Bayview offering ADA-accessible Bay Trail connections, public piers, a floating dock, a great lawn, native landscaping, youth swim programs, and free boat-building community programs.

gymsRecreation.name: Crocker Amazon Playground
gymsRecreation.description: A major sports complex in the Crocker Amazon neighborhood anchoring the southern end of McLaren Park, with soccer, baseball and softball fields, tennis and pickleball courts, basketball and bocce courts, and a clubhouse.
gymsRecreation.address: Geneva Ave & Moscow St, San Francisco, CA 94112

gymsRecreation.name: Bayview Park (Bayview Hill)
gymsRecreation.description: A 46-acre natural area park atop Bayview Hill offering sweeping views of the bay and the city, with hiking trails through native habitat; open daily 5 a.m. to midnight.
